output.answers: A list of answers, each with its question, field_id, ref and type. It is not keyed by question, so answers.Name is empty: to use an answer by its question, read fields['Name'].
output.answers_text: Beta. Every answer as a line of text, 'Question: answer', ready for an email, a message, an issue or an AI step to read when the request doesn't name particular questions.
output.email: The respondent's answer to the form's first email question, whatever its wording. Prefer it to fields[...] for an email.
output.fields: The answers keyed by each question's exact wording, such as fields['What is your email?']. The wording is the form owner's, so read only the questions the request names (and say the form must have them); a whole record in a sheet cell or a message reads as code. Every answer is text: a Yes/No question reads 'Yes' or 'No', a multiple-choice question its chosen label (several joined with ', '). A file-upload question's answer is the link Typeform keeps the file at, which is private to the Typeform account: it works as a link in an email or a sheet, but an AI step or a download may not be able to open it, so a form whose answers must be read (a CV) should also ask for the text itself or a shareable link.
output.first_name: Beta. The first word of the answer to the form's first text question that asks for a name ("Full name", "Your name"), ready for 'Hi Ada,' with no step to split the name. Empty when the form has no such question.
output.full_name: Beta. The whole answer to the form's first text question that asks for a name ("Full name", "Your name"), for a sheet column or a CRM contact with no step to put first and last names together. Empty when the form has no such question.
output.hidden: The form's hidden fields, as the link set them.
output.landed_at: When the person opened the form.
output.phone_number: The answer to the form's first phone number question, whatever its wording. Empty when the form has none.
output.rating: Beta. The number the person gave on the form's first rating question (a star rating, an opinion scale or a 'how likely are you to recommend us' score), whatever its wording, such as 3. It is a number, so compare it directly: rating <= 3 for 'a rating of 3 or lower'. Prefer it to fields[...] for a rating. Null when the form has no rating question or the person skipped it.
output.rating_out_of: Beta. The highest number the rating's scale goes to, such as 5 for five stars or 10 for a recommend score, for writing '3 out of 5'. Null when there is no rating or the form's scale could not be read.
output.rating_question: Beta. The wording of the question the rating answers, such as 'How would you rate the event?', for a task or a message that says what was rated. Empty when there is no rating.
output.score: The quiz score, for a form that keeps one.

parameters.description: The form to watch, picked from your Typeform forms. Stored as the form's ID: the code after /to/ in the form's link, such as u6nXL7 in https://example.typeform.com/to/u6nXL7.
